nodes.name: Maximal PDAGs can contain partially directed cycles
nodes.statement: An important difference between maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${}s and $\mathrm{CPDAG}$s, is that the former can contain partially directed cycles while the latter cannot. In Figure~\ref{mpdag11}, $D \rightarrow B -C-D$ and $D\rightarrow B -D$ are examples of such cycles.
nodes.statement_short: Unlike CPDAGs, maximal PDAGs can contain partially directed cycles (e.g. $D\to B-C-D$).

nodes.name: Meek's Lemma 1 fails in maximal PDAGs
nodes.statement: As a consequence, the important property of $\mathrm{CPDAG}$s which states that if $D \rightarrow B - C$ is in a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $\g[C]$, then $D \rightarrow C$ is also in $\g[C]$ \citep[Lemma 1 from][]{meek1995causal}, does not hold in maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${}s.
nodes.statement_short: The CPDAG property that $D\to B-C$ implies $D\to C$ (Meek's Lemma 1) fails in maximal PDAGs.

nodes.name: Chordality and independent orientability of undirected components of a CPDAG
nodes.statement: Furthermore, let $\g[C]_{undir}$ denote the subgraph of a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $\g[C]$ that contains only the undirected edges from $\g[C]$. It is well known that $\g[C]_{undir}$ is triangulated (chordal) and that the connected components of $\g[C]_{undir}$ can be oriented into $\mathrm{DAG}$s without unshielded colliders, independently of each other and the other edges in $\g[C]$, to form all $\mathrm{DAG}$s represented by $\g[C]$ \citep[see the proof of Theorem 4 in][]{meek1995causal}.
nodes.statement_short: The undirected subgraph of a CPDAG is chordal and its components can be oriented independently into collider-free DAGs, giving all DAGs in the class.
assumptions: let $\g[C]_{undir}$ denote the subgraph of a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $\g[C]$ that contains only the undirected edges from $\g[C]$
conclusions: $\g[C]_{undir}$ is triangulated (chordal)

the connected components of $\g[C]_{undir}$ can be oriented into $\mathrm{DAG}$s without unshielded colliders, independently of each other and the other edges in $\g[C]$, to form all $\mathrm{DAG}$s represented by $\g[C]$

nodes.name: Undirected component of a maximal PDAG need not be chordal
nodes.statement: This result is not valid in maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${}s. To see this, consider the undirected component $\g_{undir}$ of the maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$ in Figure~\ref{mpdag11}. Then $\g_{undir}$ is $A -B-C-D-A$ and is not triangulated. Orienting $B-C-D-A$ into a $\mathrm{DAG}$ always leads to at least one unshielded collider. This unshielded collider in $\g_{undir}$ must occur at $A$ or $C$, so that it is shielded in $\g$ by the edge $D\to B$. Hence, one can no longer orient $\g_{undir}$ independently of the directed edges.
nodes.statement_short: Counterexample: in the maximal PDAG of Fig. 1(c) the undirected component is a non-chordal 4-cycle that cannot be oriented independently.

nodes.name: Graph
nodes.statement: A graph $\g= (\vars,\e) $ consists of a set of nodes (variables) $ \vars=\left\lbrace X_{1},\dots,X_{p}\right\rbrace$ and a set of edges $ \e $.

nodes.name: Adjacent nodes
nodes.statement: There is at most one edge between any two nodes, and two nodes are \textit{adjacent} if an edge connects them.

nodes.name: Directed and undirected edges
nodes.statement: We call $\rightarrow$ a directed and $-$ a undirected edge.

nodes.name: Induced subgraph
nodes.statement: An \textit{induced subgraph} $\g' =(\mathbf{V'}, \mathbf{E'})$ of $\g= (\vars,\e) $ consists of a subset of nodes $\mathbf{V'} \subseteq \mathbf{V}$ and edges $\mathbf{E'} \subseteq \mathbf{E}$ where $\mathbf{E'}$ are all edges in $\mathbf{E}$ between nodes in $\mathbf{V'}$.

nodes.name: Path
nodes.statement: A \textit{path} $p$ from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$ is a sequence of distinct nodes $\langle X, \dots,Y \rangle$ in which every pair of successive nodes is adjacent.
differentia: every pair of successive nodes is adjacent

nodes.name: Node lying on a path
nodes.statement: A node $V$ \emph{lies on a path} $p$ if $V$ occurs in the sequence of nodes.

nodes.name: Endpoints and non-endpoint nodes
nodes.statement: If $p = \langle X_1, X_2, \dots , X_k, \rangle, k \ge 2$, then $X_1$ and $X_k$ are \textit{endpoints} of $p$, and any other node $X_i, 1 <i<k,$ is a \textit{non-endpoint} node on $p$.

nodes.name: Directed (causal) path
nodes.statement: A \textit{directed path} or \textit{causal path} from $X$ to $Y$ is a path from $X$ to $Y$ in which all edges are directed towards $Y$, that is $X \to \dots\to Y$.

nodes.name: Possibly directed (possibly causal) path
nodes.statement: A \textit{possibly directed path} or \textit{possibly causal path} from $X$ to $Y$ is a path from $X$ to $Y$ that does not contain an edge directed towards $X$.
differentia: does not contain an edge directed towards $X$

nodes.name: Non-causal path
nodes.statement: A \textit{non-causal} path from $X$ to $Y$ contains at least one edge directed towards $X$.

nodes.name: Path between node sets
nodes.statement: For two disjoint subsets $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ of $\mathbf{V}$, a path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ is a path from some $X \in \mathbf{X}$ to some $Y \in \mathbf{Y}$.

nodes.name: Proper path
nodes.statement: A path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ is \textit{proper} (w.r.t. $\mathbf{X}$) if only its first node is in $\mathbf{X}$.

nodes.name: Corresponding path
nodes.statement: If $\g$ and $\g^*$ are two graphs with identical adjacencies and $p$ is a path in $\g$, then the \textit{corresponding path} $\pstar$ in $\g^*$ consists of the same node sequence as $p$.

nodes.name: Directed cycle
nodes.statement: A directed path from $X$ to $Y$, together with $Y\to X$, forms a \textit{directed cycle}.

nodes.name: Partially directed cycle
nodes.statement: A \textit{partially directed cycle} is formed by a possibly directed path from $X$ to $Y$, together with $Y \to X$.

nodes.name: Subsequence of a path
nodes.statement: A \textit{subsequence} of a path $p$ is obtained by deleting some nodes from $p$ without changing the order of the remaining nodes.

nodes.name: Subpath
nodes.statement: For a path $p = \langle X_1,X_2,\dots,X_m \rangle$, the \textit{subpath} from $X_i$ to $X_k$ ($1\le i\le k\le m)$ is the path $p(X_i,X_k) = \langle X_i,X_{i+1},\dots,X_{k}\rangle$.
nodes.statement_short: $p(X_i,X_k)$ is the subpath of $p$ between $X_i$ and $X_k$.

nodes.name: Parent
nodes.statement: If $X\to Y$, then $X$ is a \textit{parent} of $Y$.

nodes.name: Sibling
nodes.statement: If $X - Y$, then $X$ is a \textit{sibling} of $Y$.

nodes.name: Ancestor and descendant
nodes.statement: If there is a causal path from $X$ to $Y$, then $X$ is an \textit{ancestor} of $Y$, and $Y$ is a \textit{descendant} of $X$. We also use the convention that every node is a descendant and an ancestor of itself.

nodes.name: Pa, Sib, An, De notation
nodes.statement: The sets of parents, siblings, ancestors and descendants of $X$ in~$\g$ are denoted by $\mathrm{Pa}(X,\g)$, $\mathrm{Sib}(X,\g)$, $\mathrm{An}(X,\g)$ and $\mathrm{De}(X,\g)$ respectively.

nodes.name: Pa, Sib, An, De of a node set
nodes.statement: For a set of nodes $\mathbf{X} \subseteq \mathbf{V}$, we let $\mathrm{Pa}(\mathbf{X},\g) = \cup_{X \in \mathbf{X}} \mathrm{Pa}(X,\g)$, with analogous definitions for $\mathrm{Sib}(\mathbf{X},\g)$, $\mathrm{An}(\mathbf{X},\g)$ and $\mathrm{De}(\mathbf{X},\g)$.

nodes.name: Collider
nodes.statement: If a path $p$ contains $X_i \rightarrow X_j \leftarrow X_k$ as a subpath, then $X_j$ is a \textit{collider} on $p$.

nodes.name: Shielded and unshielded triple
nodes.statement: A path $\langle X_{i},X_{j},X_{k} \rangle$ is an \emph{(un)shielded triple} if $ X_{i} $ and $ X_{k}$ are (not) adjacent.

nodes.name: Unshielded path
nodes.statement: A path is \textit{unshielded} if all successive triples on the path are unshielded.

nodes.name: Definite non-collider
nodes.statement: A node $X_{j}$ is a \textit{definite non-collider} on a path $p$ if there is at least one edge out of $X_{j}$ on $p$, or if $X_{i} - X_j - X_k$ is a subpath of $p$ and $\langle X_i,X_j,X_k\rangle$ is an unshielded triple.

nodes.name: Node of definite status
nodes.statement: A node is of \textit{definite status} on a path if it is a collider, a definite non-collider or an endpoint on the path.

nodes.name: Definite status path
nodes.statement: A path $p$ is of definite status if every node on $p$ is of definite status.

nodes.name: d-connecting path and blocking
nodes.statement: A definite status path \textit{p} from $X$ to $Y$ is \textit{d-connecting} given a node set $\mathbf{Z}$ ($X,Y \notin \mathbf{Z}$) if every definite non-collider on $p$ is not in $\mathbf{Z}$, and every collider on $p$ has a descendant in $\mathbf{Z}$. Otherwise, $\mathbf{Z}$ blocks $p$.

nodes.name: Directed graph
nodes.statement: A \textit{directed graph} contains only directed edges.

nodes.name: Partially directed graph
nodes.statement: A \textit{partially directed graph} may contain both directed and undirected edges.

nodes.name: Directed acyclic graph (DAG)
nodes.statement: A directed graph without directed cycles is a \textit{directed acyclic graph $(\mathrm{DAG})$}.

nodes.name: Partially directed acyclic graph (PDAG)
nodes.statement: A \textit{partially directed acyclic graph $(\mathrm{PDAG})$} is a partially directed graph without directed cycles.

nodes.name: d-separation
nodes.statement: Two disjoint node sets $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ in a $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ are \textit{d-separated} given a node set $\mathbf{Z}$ (pairwise disjoint with $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$) if and only if every path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ is blocked by $\mathbf{Z}$.

nodes.name: Markov equivalence class and CPDAG
nodes.statement: Several $\mathrm{DAG}$s can encode the same d-separation relationships. Such $\mathrm{DAG}$s form a \emph{Markov equivalence class} which is uniquely represented by a \emph{completed partially directed acyclic graph $(\mathrm{CPDAG})$} \citep{meek1995causal}.

nodes.name: Directed edges of a CPDAG are common to the class
nodes.statement: A directed edge $X \rightarrow Y$ in a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $\g[C]$ corresponds to $X \rightarrow Y$ in every $\mathrm{DAG}$ in the Markov equivalence class represented by $\g[C]$.
assumptions: A directed edge $X \rightarrow Y$ in a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $\g[C]$
conclusions: corresponds to $X \rightarrow Y$ in every $\mathrm{DAG}$ in the Markov equivalence class represented by $\g[C]$

nodes.name: Undirected edges of a CPDAG are reversible in the class
nodes.statement: For any undirected edge $X - Y$ in a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $\g[C]$, the Markov equivalence class represented by $\g[C]$ contains a $\mathrm{DAG}$ with $X \rightarrow Y$ and a $\mathrm{DAG}$ with $X \leftarrow Y$.
assumptions: any undirected edge $X - Y$ in a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $\g[C]$
conclusions: the Markov equivalence class represented by $\g[C]$ contains a $\mathrm{DAG}$ with $X \rightarrow Y$ and a $\mathrm{DAG}$ with $X \leftarrow Y$

nodes.name: PDAG represented by another PDAG
nodes.statement: A $\mathrm{PDAG}$ $\g'$ is \textit{represented} by another $\mathrm{PDAG}$ $\g$ (equivalently $\g$ represents $\g'$) if $\g'$ and $\g$ have the same adjacencies and unshielded colliders and every directed edge $X \rightarrow Y$ in $\g$ is also in $\g'$.

nodes.name: Maximally oriented PDAG (maximal PDAG)
nodes.statement: A $\mathrm{PDAG}$ $\g$ is a \textit{maximally oriented} $\mathrm{PDAG}$ if and only if the edge orientations in $\g$ are closed under the orientation rules in Figure~\ref{fig:orientationRules}. Throughout, we will refer to maximally oriented $\mathrm{PDAG}$s as \textit{maximal PDAGs}.
differentia: the edge orientations in $\g$ are closed under the orientation rules in Figure~\ref{fig:orientationRules}

nodes.name: Background knowledge R
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{R}$ be a set of required directed edges representing background knowledge.

nodes.name: ConstructMaxPDAG returns a represented maximal PDAG
nodes.statement: If Algorithm~\ref{algo} does not return a FAIL, then it returns a new maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g'$ that is represented by $\g$.
assumptions: Algorithm~\ref{algo} does not return a FAIL
conclusions: it returns a new maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g'$ that is represented by $\g$

nodes.name: Consistent background knowledge
nodes.statement: Background knowledge $\mathbf{R}$ is \textit{consistent} with maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$ if and only if Algorithm~\ref{algo} does not return a FAIL \citep{meek1995causal}.

nodes.name: ConstructMaxPDAG
nodes.statement: \TitleOfAlgo{$\mathrm{ConstructMaxPDAG}$} \KwData{maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$, background knowledge $\mathbf{R}$} \KwResult{maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g'$ or FAIL} Let $\g' = \g$\; \While{$\mathbf{R}\neq \emptyset$}{ Choose an edge $\{X \rightarrow Y\}$ in $\mathbf{R}$ \; $\mathbf{R} = \mathbf{R} \setminus \{X \rightarrow Y\}$ \; \eIf{$\{X - Y\}$ or $\{X\rightarrow Y\}$ is in $\g'$}{ Orient $\{X \rightarrow Y\}$ in $\g'$\; Close the edge orientations under the rules in Figure~\ref{fig:orientationRules} in $\g'$\; }{ FAIL\; } }
nodes.statement_short: Adds required edges from background knowledge one at a time to a maximal PDAG, closing under Meek's rules, or FAILs on a conflict.
nodes.label: algo

nodes.name: Meek's orientation rules R1-R4
nodes.statement: The orientation rules from~\cite{meek1995causal}. If the graph on the left-hand side of a rule is an induced subgraph of a $\mathrm{PDAG}$ $\g$, then \textit{orient} the blue undirected edge ({\color{blue} {\bfseries $-$}}) as shown on the right-hand side of the rule.
nodes.statement_short: Meek's rules R1-R4: orient an undirected edge whenever the left-hand pattern of a rule is an induced subgraph (patterns drawn in the figure).

nodes.name: [G]: maximal PDAGs represented by G
nodes.statement: If $\g$ is a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${}, then $[\g]$ denotes every maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} represented by $\g$.

nodes.name: Density consistent with a DAG
nodes.statement: A density $f$ of $\mathbf{V} = \{X_1,\dots,X_p\}$ is \textit{consistent} with a $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D] =(\mathbf{V},\mathbf{E})$ if it factorizes as $f(\vars)= \prod_{i=1}^{p}f(X_{i}|Pa(X_{i},\g))$ \citep{Pearl2009}.

nodes.name: Causal DAG
nodes.statement: A $\mathrm{DAG}$ is \textit{causal} if every edge $X_{i} \rightarrow X_{j}$ in $\g[D]$ represents a direct causal effect of $X_{i}$ on $X_{j}$ (wrt $\mathbf{V}$).

nodes.name: Causal PDAG
nodes.statement: A $\mathrm{PDAG}$ is \textit{causal} if it represents a causal $\mathrm{DAG}$.

nodes.name: Intervention do(x)
nodes.statement: We consider interventions $do(\mathbf{X} =\mathbf{x})$ (for $\mathbf{X}\subseteq \mathbf{V}$) or $do(\mathbf{x})$ for shorthand, which represent outside interventions that set $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{x}$ \citep{Pearl2009}.

nodes.name: Density consistent with a causal DAG
nodes.statement: A density $f$ of $\mathbf{V} = \{X_1,\dots,X_p\}$ is \textit{consistent with a causal DAG} $\g[D] =(\mathbf{V},\mathbf{E})$ if all post-intervention densities $f(\mathbf{v}|do(\mathbf{x}))$ factorize as: \begin{multline} f(\mathbf{v}|do(\mathbf{x})) = \\ = \begin{cases} \prod_{X_{i} \in \vars \setminus \mathbf{X}}f(x_{i}|\mathrm{Pa}(x_{i},\g[D])), & \text{if }\mathbf{X} =\mathbf{x}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is consistent with a causal DAG if every post-intervention density obeys the truncated factorization.

nodes.name: Truncated factorization formula (g-formula)
nodes.statement: f(\mathbf{v}|do(\mathbf{x})) = \\ = \begin{cases} \prod_{X_{i} \in \vars \setminus \mathbf{X}}f(x_{i}|\mathrm{Pa}(x_{i},\g[D])), & \text{if }\mathbf{X} =\mathbf{x}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}
nodes.statement_short: Truncated factorization: the post-intervention density is the product of the remaining conditional densities.
nodes.label: eq11

nodes.name: Density consistent with a causal PDAG
nodes.statement: A density $f$ is \textit{consistent with a causal PDAG} $\g$ if it is consistent with a causal $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$.

nodes.name: b-possibly causal path, b-non-causal path
nodes.statement: (\textbf{b-possibly causal path, b-non-causal path}) Let $p = \langle X=V_0, \dots , V_k=Y \rangle$, $k \geq 1$ be a path from node $X$ to node $Y$ in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. We say that $p$ is b-possibly causal in $\g$ if and only if no edge $V_{i} \leftarrow V_{j}, 0 \le i < j \le k$ is in $\g$. Otherwise, we say that $p$ is b-non-causal path in $\g$.

nodes.genus: path from node $X$ to node $Y$ in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$
differentia: no edge $V_{i} \leftarrow V_{j}, 0 \le i < j \le k$ is in $\g$
nodes.statement_short: A path is b-possibly causal if no edge of $\g$ points from a later node of the path to an earlier one; otherwise b-non-causal.
nodes.label: def:posdir-path

nodes.name: b-possibly causal involves off-path edges
nodes.statement: Note that Definition~\ref{def:posdir-path} involves edges that are not on $p$.

nodes.name: Soundness of b-possibly causal paths
nodes.statement: Let $\pstar$ be a path from $X$ to $Y$ in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. If $\pstar$ is b-non-causal in $\g$, then for every $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$ the corresponding path in $\g[D]$ is non-causal. By contraposition, if $p$ is a causal path in at least one $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$, then the corresponding path in $\g$ is b-possibly causal.
nodes.section: 3 POSSIBLY CAUSAL RELATIONSHIPS IN MAXIMAL PDAG{}s
nodes.statement_short: A b-non-causal path in $\g$ is non-causal in every DAG in $[\g]$; a path causal in some DAG of $[\g]$ is b-possibly causal.
assumptions: Let $\pstar$ be a path from $X$ to $Y$ in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$.
$\pstar$ is b-non-causal in $\g$
conclusions: for every $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$  the corresponding path in $\g[D]$ is non-causal
if $p$ is a causal path in at least one $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$, then the corresponding path in $\g$ is b-possibly causal
nodes.label: lemma:posdir-path

nodes.name: Results subsume CPDAG results
nodes.statement: \noindent{}Note that since every $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ is also a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${}, all results in this paper subsume existing results for $\mathrm{CPDAG}$s.

nodes.name: b-possible descendants and ancestors
nodes.statement: $(b-PossDe(\mathbf{X},\g) \text{ and }b-PossAn(\mathbf{X},\g))$ Let $\textbf{X}$ be a node set in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. Then $W$ is a b-possible descendant (b-possible ancestor) of $\mathbf{X}$ in $\g$, and we write $W \in b-PossDe(\mathbf{X},\g)$ $(W \in b-PossAn(\mathbf{X},\g))$ if and only if $W \in \mathbf{X}$ or there is a node $X \in \mathbf{X}$ and a b-possibly causal path from $X$ to $W$ ($W$ to $X$) in $\g$.
nodes.section: 3 POSSIBLY CAUSAL RELATIONSHIPS IN MAXIMAL PDAG{}s
nodes.statement_short: $W$ is a b-possible descendant (ancestor) of $\mathbf{X}$ if $W\in\mathbf{X}$ or a b-possibly causal path joins some $X\in\mathbf{X}$ to $W$ ($W$ to $X$).
nodes.label: def:posde-1

nodes.name: b-possibly causal paths in a CPDAG vs a maximal PDAG
nodes.statement: We use this example to illustrate b-possibly causal paths and b-possible descendants. Consider $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $\g[C]$ in Figure~\ref{cpdag11} and maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$ in Figure~\ref{mpdag11}. We see that $B - C - D$ is a b-possibly causal path in $\g[C]$, and a b-non-causal path in $\g$ due to $D \rightarrow B$ in $\g$. Conversely, $D-C-B$ is a b-possibly causal path in both $\g[C]$ and $\g$. Furthermore, $b-PossDe(B,\g[C]) = \{ A,B, C,D\}$ and $b-PossDe(B, \g) = \{A,B,C \}$. The b-possible descendants of $A,C$ and $D$ nodes are the same in $\g$ and $\g[C]$.
nodes.section: 3 POSSIBLY CAUSAL RELATIONSHIPS IN MAXIMAL PDAG{}s
nodes.statement_short: Adding $D\to B$ makes $B-C-D$ b-non-causal and removes $D$ from $b-PossDe(B,\g)$.
nodes.label: ex:allpossdec

nodes.name: Argument for linear-time b-possible descendants
nodes.statement: To solve this issue, we use Lemma~\ref{lemma:unshielded-analog} (analogous to \citealp[Lemma~B.1 in][]{zhang2008completeness}) to only consider paths which are unshielded and hence, of definite status. We then only need consider the edges which are on the definite status paths (Lemma~\ref{lemma:def-stat-posdir}).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to unshielded (definite status) paths via Lemma 3.6, whose b-possibly causal status depends only on their own edges (Lemma 3.5).

nodes.name: Linear-time computation of b-possible descendants
nodes.statement: Thus, the task of finding all b-possible descendants (ancestors) of $\mathbf{X}$ in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g = (\mathbf{V},\mathbf{E})$ can be done using a depth first search algorithm with computational complexity $O(|\mathbf{V}| + |\mathbf{E}|)$.
nodes.statement_short: All b-possible descendants/ancestors of $\mathbf{X}$ can be found by depth-first search in $O(|V|+|E|)$.
assumptions: a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g = (\mathbf{V},\mathbf{E})$
conclusions: the task of finding all b-possible descendants (ancestors) of $\mathbf{X}$ in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g = (\mathbf{V},\mathbf{E})$ can be done using a depth first search algorithm with computational complexity $O(|\mathbf{V}| + |\mathbf{E}|)$

nodes.name: Local characterization of b-possibly causal definite status paths
nodes.statement: Let $\pstar = \langle V_1, \dots , V_k \rangle$ be a definite status path in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. Then $\pstar$ is b-possibly causal if and only if there is no $V_i \leftarrow V_{i+1}$, for $i \in \{1,\dots, k-1\}$ in $\g$.
nodes.statement_short: A definite status path is b-possibly causal iff none of its own edges points backwards.
assumptions: Let $\pstar = \langle V_1, \dots , V_k \rangle$ be a definite status path in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$.
conclusions: $\pstar$ is b-possibly causal if and only if there is no $V_i \leftarrow V_{i+1}$, for $i \in \{1,\dots, k-1\}$  in $\g$
equivalent_conditions: there is no $V_i \leftarrow V_{i+1}$, for $i \in \{1,\dots, k-1\}$  in $\g$
nodes.label: lemma:def-stat-posdir

nodes.name: Unshielded b-possibly causal subsequence
nodes.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be distinct nodes in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. If $p$ is s a b-possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$, then a subsequence $\pstar$ of $p$ forms a b-possibly causal unshielded path from $X$ to $Y$ in~$\g$.
nodes.statement_short: Every b-possibly causal path contains a subsequence that is an unshielded b-possibly causal path with the same endpoints.
assumptions: Let $X$ and $Y$ be distinct nodes in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$.
$p$ is s a b-possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g$
conclusions: a subsequence $\pstar$ of $p$ forms a b-possibly causal unshielded path from $X$ to $Y$ in~$\g$
nodes.label: lemma:unshielded-analog

nodes.name: Standing setting: causal maximal PDAG and disjoint node sets
nodes.statement: Throughout, let $\g=(\vars,\e)$ represent a causal maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${}, and let $\mathbf{X}$, $\mathbf{Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint subsets of $\vars$.
nodes.section: 4 ESTIMATING TOTAL CAUSAL EFFECTS WITH MAXIMAL PDAG{}S

nodes.name: Adjustment set
nodes.statement: {(\textbf{Adjustment set})} Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. Then $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g$ if for any density $f$ consistent with $\g$ we have \begin{equation} f(\mathbf{y}|do(\mathbf{x}))= \begin{cases} f(\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}) & \text{if }\mathbf{Z} = \emptyset,\\ \int_{\mathbf{z}}f(\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x,z})f(\mathbf{z})d\mathbf{z} & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \nonumber \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set for $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ if the interventional density equals the covariate-adjusted observational formula for every consistent density.
nodes.label: defadjustmentmpdag

nodes.name: Total causal effect as a regression coefficient under linear SEMs
nodes.statement: Under the assumption that the density consistent with the underlying causal $\mathrm{DAG}$ can be generated by a linear structural equation model (SEM) with additive noise \citep[see Ch.5 in][for definition of SEMs]{Pearl2009}, covariate adjustment allows the researcher to estimate the total causal effect by performing one multiple linear regression \citep[see][for the non-Gaussian noise result]{nandy2014estimating}. In this setting, if $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set relative to some nodes $X$, $Y$ in $\g$, then the coefficient of $X$ in the linear regression of $Y$ on $X$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ is the total causal effect of $X$ on $Y$.
nodes.statement_short: Under a linear SEM, the coefficient of $X$ in the regression of $Y$ on $X$ and an adjustment set $\mathbf{Z}$ is the total causal effect.
assumptions: the density consistent with the underlying causal $\mathrm{DAG}$ can be generated by a linear structural equation model (SEM) with additive noise
$\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set relative to some nodes $X$, $Y$ in $\g$
conclusions: the coefficient of $X$ in the linear regression of $Y$ on $X$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ is the total causal effect of $X$ on $Y$

nodes.name: b-forbidden set
nodes.statement_short: The b-forbidden set: all b-possible descendants of non-$\mathbf{X}$ nodes on proper b-possibly causal paths from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$.
nodes.label: def:forbidden nodes

nodes.name: b-adjustment criterion
nodes.statement: {(\textbf{b-adjustment criterion})} Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. Then $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g$ if:\vspace{-0.4cm} \begin{enumerate}[label = (\cctext*), leftmargin=0.5cm,align=left] \item all proper b-possibly causal paths from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ start with a directed edge out of $\mathbf{X}$ in $\g$, \item $\mathbf{Z} \cap \bfb{\g} = \emptyset$, \item all proper b-non-causal definite status paths from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ are blocked by $\mathbf{Z}$~in~$\g$. \end{enumerate}
differentia: all proper b-possibly causal paths from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ start with a directed edge out of $\mathbf{X}$ in $\g$
all proper b-non-causal definite status paths from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ are blocked by $\mathbf{Z}$~in~$\g$
nodes.statement_short: Three conditions: b-amenability, $\mathbf{Z}$ avoids the b-forbidden set, and $\mathbf{Z}$ blocks all proper b-non-causal definite status paths.
nodes.label: def:gac-pdag

nodes.name: b-adjustment criterion is sound and complete
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. Then $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set (Definition~\ref{defadjustmentmpdag}) relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$ if and only if $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion (Definition~\ref{def:gac-pdag}) relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$.
nodes.statement_short: In a causal maximal PDAG, $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set iff it satisfies the b-adjustment criterion.
assumptions: Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$.
conclusions: $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set (Definition~\ref{defadjustmentmpdag}) relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$ if and only if $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion (Definition~\ref{def:gac-pdag}) relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$
equivalent_conditions: $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set (Definition~\ref{defadjustmentmpdag}) relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$
$\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion (Definition~\ref{def:gac-pdag}) relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$
nodes.label: theorem:gac-pdag

nodes.name: b-Adjust set
nodes.statement: $(\badjustb{\g})$ Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. We define \begin{align} &\badjustb{\g}= \nonumber \\ &b-PossAn(\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y}, \g)\setminus(\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y} \cup \bfb{\g}). \nonumber \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $b$-Adjust: b-possible ancestors of $\mathbf{X}\cup\mathbf{Y}$ minus $\mathbf{X}$, $\mathbf{Y}$ and the b-forbidden set.
nodes.label: def:constr-set-mpdag

nodes.name: Constructive b-adjustment set
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. There exists a set that satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$ if and only if $\badjustb{\g}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$.
nodes.statement_short: An adjustment set exists iff the explicit set $b$-Adjust$(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y},\g)$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion.
assumptions: Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$.
conclusions: There exists a set that satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$ if and only if $\badjustb{\g}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$
equivalent_conditions: There exists a set that satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$
$\badjustb{\g}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$
nodes.label: theorem:constructive-set-mpdag

nodes.name: b-adjustment criterion on a CPDAG and two maximal PDAGs
nodes.statement: We use this example to illustrate the b-adjustment criterion. Consider Figure~\ref{figex2} with a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $\g[C]$ in (a), and two maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${}s $\g_{1}$ and $\g_{2}$ in $[\g]$ in (b) and (c). Maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g_{1}$ ($\g_{2}$) can be obtained from $\g[C]$ by adding $V_1 \rightarrow X$ ($Y \rightarrow X$) as background knowledge and completing the orientation rules from Figure~\ref{fig:orientationRules}. $\g[C]$ is not b-amenable relative to $(X,Y)$ due to $X - Y$ and $X -V_2 -Y$. Hence, there is no adjustment set (no set satisfies Definition~\ref{def:gac-pdag}) relative to $(X,Y)$ in $\g$. On the other hand, $\g_{1}$ is b-amenable relative to $(X,Y)$ and $\bbf{\g_{1}} = \{ V_2, Y\}$. Since there are no b-non-causal paths from $X$ to $Y$ in $\g_{1}$ any set of nodes disjoint with $\bbf{\g_{1}} \cup \{X,Y\}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(X,Y)$. Hence, all valid adjustment sets relative to $(X,Y)$ in $\g_{1}$ are $\emptyset$ and $\{V_1\}$. Maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g_2$ is also b-amenable relative to $(X,Y)$ (since $X-V_2 -Y$ is a b-non-causal path). Since $X \leftarrow Y$ is in $\g_{2}$, $\bbf{\g_{2}} = \emptyset$. However, since $X \leftarrow Y$ is a proper b-non-causal definite status path from $X$ to $Y$ that cannot be blocked by any set of nodes, there is no adjustment set (no set satisfies Definition~\ref{def:gac-pdag}) relative to $(X,Y)$ in $\g_2$. Nevertheless, since $Y \notin b-PossDe(X,\g_{2})$, we can conclude that the total causal effect of $X$ on $Y$ in $\g_{2}$ is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Background knowledge can make a non-amenable CPDAG amenable (adjustment sets $\emptyset$, $\{V_1\}$) or reveal a zero effect.
nodes.label: ex2

nodes.name: b-blocking can be checked in one DAG
nodes.statement: If $\g$ is b-amenable and $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-forbidden set condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$, then in order to verify that $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-blocking condition{} in $\g$ it is enough to verify that $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-blocking condition{} in one $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$ (\ref{l:eqb3-pdag} in Lemma~\ref{lemma:eqb-pdag} in the supplement).
nodes.statement_short: Under b-amenability and the forbidden-set condition, b-blocking in $\g$ is equivalent to b-blocking in any single DAG of $[\g]$.
assumptions: $\g$ is b-amenable
$\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-forbidden set condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$
conclusions: it is enough to verify that $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-blocking condition{} in one $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$

nodes.name: Finding one DAG in [G] in O(|V||E|)
nodes.statement: The computational complexity of finding one $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$ is $O(|\mathbf{V}||\mathbf{E}|)$, as shown in \cite{dorTarsi92}.
conclusions: The computational complexity of finding one $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$ is $O(|\mathbf{V}||\mathbf{E}|)$

nodes.name: Linear-time verification of adjustment in a DAG
nodes.statement: The computational complexity of verifying whether a set satisfies the b-adjustment criterion in $\g[D]$ is $O(|\mathbf{V}| +|\mathbf{E}|)$, as shown in \cite{vanconstructing}.
nodes.origin_citation: van der Zander et al. (constructing adjustment sets)
conclusions: The computational complexity of verifying whether a set satisfies the b-adjustment criterion in $\g[D]$  is $O(|\mathbf{V}| +|\mathbf{E}|)$

nodes.name: Polynomial-delay listing of adjustment sets in a DAG
nodes.statement: Furthermore, the computational complexity of listing all or all minimal adjustment sets in $\g[D]$, is at most polynomial in $|\mathbf{V}|$ and $|\mathbf{E}|$ per output set, as shown in \cite{vanconstructing}.
nodes.origin_citation: van der Zander et al. (constructing adjustment sets)
conclusions: the computational complexity of listing all or all minimal adjustment sets in $\g[D]$, is at most polynomial in $|\mathbf{V}|$ and $|\mathbf{E}|$ per output set

nodes.name: Polynomial complexity of adjustment in maximal PDAGs
nodes.statement: The complexity of verifying the b-blocking condition{} in $\g$ when exploiting the results of Lemma~\ref{lemma:eqb-pdag}, \cite{dorTarsi92} and \cite{vanconstructing} is polynomial in $|\mathbf{V}|$ and $|\mathbf{E}|$ and listing all or all minimal adjustment sets in $\g$ is polynomial in $|\mathbf{V}|$ and $|\mathbf{E}|$ per output set.
nodes.statement_short: Combining Lemma C.3 with Dor-Tarsi and van der Zander et al., b-blocking can be verified, and adjustment sets listed, in polynomial time in maximal PDAGs.
conclusions: The complexity of verifying the b-blocking condition{} in $\g$ when exploiting the results of Lemma~\ref{lemma:eqb-pdag}, \cite{dorTarsi92} and \cite{vanconstructing} is polynomial in $|\mathbf{V}|$ and $|\mathbf{E}|$
listing all or all minimal adjustment sets in $\g$ is polynomial in $|\mathbf{V}|$ and $|\mathbf{E}|$ per output set

nodes.name: Global IDA
nodes.statement: In order to estimate the possible total causal effects of a node $X$ on a node $Y$ based on a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $\g[C]$ one can consider listing all $\mathrm{DAG}$s in $[\g[C]]$ and estimating the total causal effect of $X$ on $Y$ in each. Since this effect may differ between different $\mathrm{DAG}$s in $\g$, the output of such an algorithm is a multi-set of possible total causal effects of $X$ on $Y$.
nodes.section: 4.2 IDA AND JOINT-IDA IN MAXIMAL PDAG{}s
nodes.statement_short: Global IDA: enumerate all DAGs in the class and estimate the effect of $X$ on $Y$ in each, giving a multi-set.

nodes.name: Parent set is an adjustment set
nodes.statement: If $Y$ is not a parent of $X$ in a causal $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$, it is well known that $\mathrm{Pa}(X,\g[D])$ is an adjustment set relative to $(X,Y)$ in $\g[D]$ \citep{Pearl2009}.
nodes.section: 4.2 IDA AND JOINT-IDA IN MAXIMAL PDAG{}s
assumptions: $Y$ is not a parent of $X$ in a causal $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$
conclusions: $\mathrm{Pa}(X,\g[D])$ is an adjustment set relative to $(X,Y)$ in $\g[D]$

nodes.name: Semi-local (joint-)IDA parent sets in maximal PDAGs
nodes.statement: \TitleOfAlgo{Semi-locally find all joint parent sets of $\mathbf{X} = (X_1,\dots ,X_k), k \ge 1,$ in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$.} \KwData{maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$, $\mathbf{X} = \{X_1,\dots ,X_k\}, k \ge 1$} \KwResult{Multi-set $\mathbf{PossPa}$ of all joint parent sets of $\mathbf{X}$} $\mathbf{PossPa}=\emptyset$; \\ $\mathbf{Sib_1} =\{ A: A - X_1 \text{ in } \g \}$; \\ \If{$k >1$}{ $\mathbf{Sib}_i = \{ A: A - X_i \text{ in } \g \} \setminus \{X_1, \dots, X_{i-1} \}$; \\ } \ForAll{$\mathbf{S}_i \subseteq \mathbf{Sib}_i$, $i = 1 , \dots , k$,}{ $ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{LocalBg} = &\cup_{i=1}^k \{ A \rightarrow X_i : A \in \mathbf{S}_i\} \cup \\ &\cup_{i=1}^k \{ X_i \rightarrow A : A \in \mathbf{Sib}_i \setminus \mathbf{S}_i\}; \end{aligned}$\\ \If{$\mathrm{ConstructMaxPDAG}(\g,\mathbf{LocalBg}) \neq \text{FAIL}$}{ add $(\mathrm{Pa}(X_1,\g) \cup \mathbf{S}_1 ,\dots , \mathrm{Pa}(X_k,\g) \cup \mathbf{S}_k)$ to $\mathbf{PossPa}$;\\ } } \vspace{-.3cm}
nodes.section: 4.2 IDA AND JOINT-IDA IN MAXIMAL PDAG{}s
nodes.statement_short: For each choice of sibling subsets, impose them as local background knowledge and keep the resulting joint parent sets that ConstructMaxPDAG accepts.
output: Multi-set $\mathbf{PossPa}$ of all joint parent sets of $\mathbf{X}$
nodes.label: algo:ida

nodes.name: Runtime of semi-local IDA vs local IDA and semi-local joint-IDA
nodes.statement: In this case, Algorithm~\ref{algo:ida} will in general be slower than local IDA, as it requires closing the orientation rules of \cite{meek1995causal}, but also in general somewhat faster than semi-local joint IDA, since it does not require orienting an entire undirected component of the $\mathrm{CPDAG}$.
nodes.section: 4.2 IDA AND JOINT-IDA IN MAXIMAL PDAG{}s
nodes.statement_short: On CPDAGs the new algorithm is generally slower than local IDA but somewhat faster than semi-local joint-IDA.

nodes.name: Local IDA fails on maximal PDAGs
nodes.statement: Consider the maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$ in Figure~\ref{mpdag11}. Suppose we want to estimate the total causal effect of $C$ on $A$ in $\g$. All possible parent sets of $C$ according to Algorithm~\ref{algo:ida} are: $\emptyset , \{D\}, \{B,D\}$. These are also all possible parent sets of $C$ according to Figure~\ref{alldagmpdag}. We now show that local IDA cannot be applied. For every $\mathbf{S} \subseteq \mathrm{Sib}(C,\g)$, local IDA from \cite{MaathuisKalischBuehlmann09} orients $S -C$ as $S \rightarrow C$ for every $S \in \mathbf{S}$. If this does not introduce a new unshielded collider $\rightarrow C \leftarrow$ it returns $\mathrm{Pa}(C,\g) \cup \mathbf{S}$ as a valid parent set. Local IDA returns the following sets as the possible parent sets of $C$: $\emptyset , \{B\}, \{D\}, \{B,D\}$. However, parent set $\{B\}$ means adding $B \rightarrow C$ and $C \rightarrow D$ and this introduces a cycle due to $D \rightarrow B$. Hence, $\{B\}$ will never be a parent set of $C$ in $[\g[C]]$ and local IDA is not valid for maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${}s.
nodes.statement_short: Local IDA returns the invalid parent set $\{B\}$ for $C$ in the maximal PDAG of Fig. 1(c).
nodes.label: ex:local-ida

nodes.name: Semi-local joint-IDA fails on maximal PDAGs
nodes.statement: Consider again the maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$ in Figure~\ref{mpdag11}. Suppose we want to estimate the total causal effect of $(C,D)$ on $A$ in $\g$. All possible joint parent sets of $(C,D)$ according to Algorithm~\ref{algo:ida} are: $(\emptyset,\{C\}), (\{D\},\emptyset), (\{B,D\},\emptyset), (\{B,D\},\{A\})$. These are also all possible joint parent sets of $(C,D)$ according to Figure~\ref{alldagmpdag}. Semi-local joint-IDA from \cite{nandy2014estimating} would attempt to learn all possible joint parent sets of $(C,D)$ by orienting the undirected component $B-C-D-A$ on $\g$ into all possible $\mathrm{DAG}$s without unshielded colliders. However, it is not possible to orient $B-C-D-A$ into a $\mathrm{DAG}$ without creating an unshielded collider. Hence, semi-local joint-IDA is not valid for maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${}s.
nodes.statement_short: Semi-local joint-IDA cannot orient the non-chordal component $B-C-D-A$ without an unshielded collider.
nodes.label: ex:semiloc-jida

nodes.name: Background knowledge increases identifiability via adjustment
nodes.statement: We see that without any background knowledge around $90\%$ of all total causal effects could be identified via adjustment, while around $70\%$ of the non-zero total causal effects could be identified via adjustment. When the proportion of background knowledge increases, the fraction of total causal effects that we identify via adjustment increases, both for all total causal effects and for the non-zero total causal effects.
nodes.statement_short: Simulations: ~90% of effects (70% of non-zero) identifiable by adjustment without background knowledge, increasing with more.

nodes.name: Background knowledge reduces the number of unique IDA estimates
nodes.statement: When including background knowledge, the fraction of multi-sets with exactly one unique estimate gradually increases.
nodes.statement_short: Simulations: with more background knowledge, more IDA multi-sets have a single unique estimate.

nodes.name: Complete orientation rules for PAGs with background knowledge
nodes.statement: It would be interesting to extend our methods to settings with hidden variables, e.g., considering partial ancestral graphs ($\mathrm{PAG}$s; \citealp{richardson2002ancestral,ali2012towards}) with background knowledge. An important missing link for such an extension is a clear understanding of $\mathrm{PAG}$s with background knowledge. In particular, one would need to develop complete orientation rules for $\mathrm{PAG}$s with background knowledge, analogous to the work of \cite{meek1995causal}.
nodes.statement_short: Extend the methods to hidden variables; requires complete orientation rules for PAGs with background knowledge.

nodes.name: Reversed path -p
nodes.statement: If $p = \langle X_1, X_2, \dots , X_k, \rangle, k \ge 2$ is a path, then with $-p$ we denote the path $\langle X_k, \dots , X_2, X_1 \rangle$.

nodes.name: Length of a path
nodes.statement: The \textit{length} of a path equals the number of edges on the path.

nodes.name: Concatenation of paths
nodes.statement: We denote the concatenation of paths by $\oplus$, so that for example $p = p(X_1,X_{m}) \oplus p(X_{m},X_{k})$ for $1 \le m \le k$.

nodes.name: Distance-from-Z
nodes.statement: (\textbf{Distance-from-$\mathbf{Z}$}) Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. Let $p$ be a path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ in~$\g$ such that every collider $C$ on $p$ has a b-possibly causal path to $\mathbf{Z}$. Define the $distance-from-\!{\mathbf{Z}}$ of collider $C$ to be the length of a shortest b-possibly causal path from $C$ to $\mathbf{Z}$, and define the $distance-from-\!{\mathbf{Z}}$ of $p$ to be the sum of the distances from $\mathbf{Z}$ of the colliders on $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Distance-from-$\mathbf{Z}$ of a path: sum over its colliders of the length of a shortest b-possibly causal path to $\mathbf{Z}$.
nodes.label: def:distance from Z

nodes.name: Orientation of a sibling edge makes new arrowheads descendants
nodes.statement: \citep[Lemma~A.7 in][]{ernestroth2016} Let $X$ and $Y$ be nodes in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$ such that $X - Y$ is in $\g$. Let $\g' = \mathrm{ConstructMaxPDAG}(\g,\{X \rightarrow Y\})$. For any $Z,W \in \mathbf{V}$ if $Z \rightarrow W$ is in $\g'$ and $Z -W$ is in $\g$, then $W \in \mathrm{De}(Y,\g')$.
nodes.origin_citation: Lemma A.7 in Ernest et al. 2016
assumptions: Let $X$ and $Y$ be nodes in a  maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$ such that $X - Y$ is in $\g$.
Let $\g' = \mathrm{ConstructMaxPDAG}(\g,\{X \rightarrow Y\})$.
$Z \rightarrow W$ is in $\g'$ and $Z -W$ is in $\g$
conclusions: $W \in \mathrm{De}(Y,\g')$
nodes.label: lemma:alwaydesc

nodes.name: No new edges into a node
nodes.statement: \citep[cf.\ Lemma~A.8 in][]{ernestroth2016} Let $X$ be a node in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. Then there is a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g'$ in $[\g]$ such that $X \rightarrow S$ is in $\g'$ for all $S \in \mathrm{Sib}(X,\g)$.
nodes.origin_citation: cf. Lemma A.8 in Ernest et al. 2016
assumptions: Let $X$ be a node in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$.
conclusions: there is a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g'$ in $[\g]$ such that $X \rightarrow S$ is in $\g'$ for all $S \in \mathrm{Sib}(X,\g)$
nodes.label: lemma:no-new-into

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: Since $\pstar = \langle X=V_0, \dots , V_k=Y \rangle$, $k \geq 1$ is b-non-causal in $\g$, we have $V_i \leftarrow V_j$ in $\g$ for some $i,j$ such that $ 0 \le i < j \le k$. Let $\g[D]$ be an arbitrary $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$ and let $p$ be the path corresponding to $\pstar$ in $\g[D]$. Since $V_i \leftarrow V_j$ in $\g[D]$, $p(V_i, V_j)$ is non-causal from $V_i$ to $V_j$ in $\g[D]$. Hence, $p$ is b-non-causal in $\g[D]$.
nodes.statement_short: A backward edge $V_i\leftarrow V_j$ of $\g$ persists in every DAG of $[\g]$, making the subpath non-causal.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: One direction is trivial and we only prove that if there is no $V_i \leftarrow V_{i+1}$, for $i \in \{1,\dots, k-1\}$ in $\g$, then $\pstar$ is b-possibly causal in $\g$. Suppose for a contradiction that $\pstar$ is b-non-causal, that is, there is an edge $V_{j} \leftarrow V_{r}$, for $1 \le j < r \le k$, where $r \neq j +1$. Since there is no $V_i \leftarrow V_{i+1}$ for any $i \in \{1,\dots, k-1\}$ in $\g$, $V_i - V_{i+1}$ or $V_i \rightarrow V_{i+1}$ is in $\g$ for every $i \in \{1,\dots, k-1\}$. Let $\g[D]$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$ that contains $V_1 \rightarrow V_2$ and let $p$ be the path corresponding to $\pstar$ in $\g[D]$. Since $\pstar$ is of definite status in $\g$ and since no $V_i \leftarrow V_{i+1}$, $i \in \{1,\dots, k-1\}$ is in $\g$, it follows that $\pstar$ contains only definite non-colliders. Then since $V_1 \rightarrow V_2$ is on $p$, $p$ is a causal path in $\g[D]$. But then $p(V_{j},V_{r})$ together with $V_j \leftarrow V_r$ create a directed cycle in $\g[D]$.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a long backward edge plus a causal orientation of the definite status path creates a directed cycle in some DAG.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction on the length of $p$. Let $p=\langle X= V_1, \dots , V_k =Y \rangle$. Suppose that $k=3$. Then either $p$ is unshielded, or there is an edge $X - Y$ or $X \rightarrow Y$ in $\g$ ($X \leftarrow Y$ is not in $\g$ since $p$ is b-possibly causal). For the induction step suppose that the lemma holds for paths of length $n-1$ and let $k=n$. Then either $p$ is unshielded, or there is a node $V_i$, $i >1$ on $p$, such that $V_{i-1} - V_{i+1}$ or $V_{i-1} \rightarrow V_{i+1}$ is in $\g$ ($V_{i-1} \leftarrow V_{i+1}$ is not in $\g$ since $p$ is b-possibly causal ). Then $p' = p(X,V_{i-1}) \oplus \langle V_{i-1}, V_{i+1} \rangle \oplus p(V_{i+1},Y)$ is a b-possibly causal path from $X$ to $Y$ of length $n-1$ and $p'$ is a subsequence of $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on path length: shortcut a shielded triple by its chord, which cannot point backwards.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.1
nodes.statement: The following lemma is analogous to Lemma 7.2 in \cite{maathuis2013generalized} and follows directly from our definitions of b-possibly causal paths and definite status paths.
nodes.statement_short: Follows directly from the definitions (analogous to Lemma 7.2 of Maathuis & Colombo).

nodes.name: Directed edge on a b-possibly causal definite status path propagates
nodes.statement: Let $p =\langle V_1, \dots , V_k \rangle$ be a b-possibly causal definite status path in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. If there is a node $i \in \{1, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $V_i \rightarrow V_{i+1}$, then $p(V_i, V_k)$ is a causal path in $\g$.
assumptions: Let $p =\langle V_1, \dots , V_k \rangle$ be a b-possibly causal definite status path in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$.
there is a node $i \in \{1, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $V_i \rightarrow V_{i+1}$
conclusions: $p(V_i, V_k)$ is a causal path in $\g$
nodes.label: lemma:unshielded-edgeanalog

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.4
nodes.statement: This proof is basically the same as the proof of Theorem 5 from \cite{perkovic16}, except that instead of using Lemmas 8, 9 and 10 from \cite{perkovic16}, we need to use Lemmas ~\ref{lemma:amen-pdag}, \ref{lemma:eqpdag} and \ref{lemma:eqb-pdag}. We give the entire proof for completeness. Suppose first that $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in the maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. We need to show that $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set (Definition~\ref{defadjustmentmpdag}) relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in every $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$. By applying Lemmas~\ref{lemma:amen-pdag},~\ref{lemma:eqpdag} and~\ref{lemma:eqb-pdag} in turn, it directly follows that $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in any $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$. Since the b-adjustment criterion reduces to the adjustment criterion \citep{shpitser2012validity,shpitser2012avalidity} in $\mathrm{DAG}$s and the adjustment criterion is sound for $\mathrm{DAG}$s, $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g[D]$. To prove the other direction, suppose that $\mathbf{Z}$ does not satisfy the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g$. First, suppose that $\g$ violates the b-amenability condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$. Then by Lemma~\ref{lemma:amen-pdag}, there is no adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\g$. Otherwise, suppose $\g$ is b-amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$. Then $\mathbf{Z}$ violates the b-forbidden set condition{} or \expandafter\ignorespaces the b-blocking condition{}. We need to show $\mathbf{Z}$ is not an adjustment set in at least one $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$. Suppose $\mathbf{Z}$ violates \expandafter\ignorespaces the forbidden set condition. Then by Lemma~\ref{lemma:eqpdag}, it follows that there exists a $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$ such that $\mathbf{Z}$ does not satisfy the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g[D]$. Since the b-adjustment criterion reduces to the adjustment criterion \citep{shpitser2012validity,shpitser2012avalidity} in $\mathrm{DAG}$s and the adjustment criterion is complete for $\mathrm{DAG}$s, it follows that $\mathbf{Z}$ is not an adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g[D]$. Otherwise, suppose $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies \expandafter\ignorespaces the forbidden set condition, but violates \expandafter\ignorespaces the b-blocking condition{}. Then by Lemma~\ref{lemma:eqb-pdag}, it follows that there is a $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$ such that $\mathbf{Z}$ does not satisfy the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g[D]$. Since the b-adjustment criterion reduces to the adjustment criterion \citep{shpitser2012validity,shpitser2012avalidity} in $\mathrm{DAG}$s and the adjustment criterion is complete for $\mathrm{DAG}$s, it follows that $\mathbf{Z}$ is not an adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g[D]$.
nodes.statement_short: Soundness: Lemmas C.1-C.3 transfer the criterion to every DAG in $[\g]$; completeness: each violated condition yields a DAG where $\mathbf{Z}$ fails the DAG adjustment criterion.

nodes.name: Non-b-amenability implies no adjustment set
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. If $\g$ violates the b-amenability condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$, then there is no adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\g$.
assumptions: Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$.
$\g$ violates the b-amenability condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$

nodes.label: lemma:amen-pdag

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.1
nodes.statement: This lemma is related to Lemma~8 from \cite{perkovic16}. The proofs are not the same due to the differences between $\mathrm{CPDAG}$s and maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${}s. We will point out where the two proofs diverge. Suppose that $\g$ violates the b-amenability condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$. We will show that in this case one can find $\mathrm{DAG}$s $\g[D]_1$ and $\g[D]_2$ in $[\g]$, such that there is no set that satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in both $\g[D]_1$ and $\g[D]_2$. Since $\g$ is not b-amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$, there is a proper b-possibly causal path $\pstar[q]$ from a node $X \in \mathbf{X}$ to a node $Y \in \mathbf{Y}$ that starts with a undirected edge. Let $\pstar[q'] = \langle X= V_0,V_1,\dots,V_k=Y\rangle, k \ge 1$ (where $V_1 = Y$ is allowed) be a shortest subsequence of $\pstar[q]$ such that $\pstar[q']$ is also a proper b-possibly causal path that starts with a undirected edge in~$\g$. Suppose first that $\pstar[q']$ is of definite status in $\g$. Let $\g[D]_1$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$ that contains $X \rightarrow V_1$ and let $\g[D]_2$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$ that has no additional edges into $V_1$ as compared to $\g$ (Lemma~\ref{lemma:no-new-into}). Then the path corresponding to $\pstar[q']$ in $\g[D]_1$ is causal, whereas the path corresponding to $\pstar[q']$ in $\g[D]_2$ is b-non-causal and contains no colliders. Hence, no set can satisfy both the b-forbidden set condition{} in $\g[D]_1$ and the b-blocking condition{} in $\g[D]_2$ relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$. Otherwise, $\pstar[q']$ is not of definite status in $\g$. In the proof of Lemma 8 from \cite{perkovic16}, the authors show that if $\pstar[q']$ is not of definite status, this leads to a contradiction. However, $\pstar[q']$ can be of non-definite status in $\g$ and this is where the proofs diverge. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:unshielded-analog}, $\pstar[q'](V_1,Y)$ must be unshielded and hence, of definite status in $\g$, since otherwise we can choose a shorter b-possibly causal path. Since $\pstar[q']$ is not of definite status and $\pstar[q'](V_1,Y)$ is of definite status, it follows that $V_1$ is not of definite status on $\pstar[q']$. Then $\langle X, V_1, V_2 \rangle$ is a shielded triple. By choice of $\pstar[q']$, $X - V_1$ is in $\g$. Additionally, since $V_1$ is not of definite status on $\pstar[q']$, $V_1 - V_2$ must be in $\g$. This implies that $X - V_1 -V_2$ is in $\g$ and $X \in \mathrm{Adj}(V_2,\g)$. Moreover, we must have $X \to V_2$, since $X - V_2$ contradicts the choice of $\pstar[q']$, and $X \leftarrow V_2$ contradicts that $\pstar[q']$ is b-possibly causal in $\g$. Let $\g[D]_1$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $\g$ that has no additional edges into $V_1$ as compared to $\g$ (Lemma~\ref{lemma:no-new-into}). Let $q_1$ be the path corresponding to $\pstar[q']$ in $\g[D]_1$. Then $q_1$ is of the form $X \leftarrow V_1 \rightarrow V_2 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow Y$ in $\g[D]_1$. Since $X \rightarrow V_2 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow Y$ is a proper causal path in $\g[D]_1$, $\{V_2, \dots, V_{k-1}\} \subseteq \bfb{\g[D]_{1}}$. Hence, any set that satisfies the b-blocking condition{} and the b-forbidden set condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g[D]_{1}$ must contain $V_1$ and not $\{V_2,\dots,V_{k-1}$. Let $\g[D]_2$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $\g$ that has no additional edges into $V_2$ as compared to $\g$ (Lemma~\ref{lemma:no-new-into}). Let $q_2$ be the path corresponding to $\pstar[q']$ in $\g[D]_2$. Since $X \rightarrow V_2 \rightarrow V_1$ is in $\g[D]_2$, $X \rightarrow V_1$ is in $\g[D]_2$ (Rule $R2$). Then $q_2$ is of the form $ X \rightarrow V_1 \leftarrow V_2 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow Y$ in $\g[D]_2$. Hence, any set that satisfies the b-forbidden set condition{} and the b-blocking condition{} {} relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g[D]_{1}$, violates the b-blocking condition{} {} relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g[D]_{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a shortest proper b-possibly causal path starting undirected and build two DAGs in $[\g]$ whose adjustment requirements conflict. The non-definite-status case, new for maximal PDAGs, uses rule R2.

nodes.name: Forbidden-set condition transfers to every DAG

conclusions: the following statements are equivalent:

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.2
nodes.statement:
This lemma is related to Lemma~10 from \cite{perkovic16}. By Lemma~ef{lemma:posdir-path} $ fb{\g[D]} \subseteq  fb{\g}$ hence, ef{l:eqa1-pdag}$\Rightarrow$ef{l:eqa2-pdag} holds. We now prove $
eg$~ef{l:eqa1-pdag}$\Rightarrow
eg$~ef{l:eqa2-pdag}. Let $V \in \mathbf{Z} \cap  fb{\g}$. Then $V \in b-PossDe(W,\g)$ for some $W= V_i$ on a proper b-possibly causal path $p = \langle X=V_0, V_1,\dots, V_k=Y angle, 1 \le i \le k$ from $X \in \mathbf{X}$ to $Y \in \mathbf{Y}$. Let $q=p(X,W)$, $r=p(W,Y)$ and let $s$ be a b-possibly causal path from $W$ to $V$, where $r$ and $s$ are allowed to be of zero length (if $W=Y$ and/or $W=V$). Let $q'$, $r'$ and $s'$ be subsequences of $q$, $r$ and $s$ that form unshielded b-possibly causal paths, with $r'$ and $s'$ possibly of zero length (Lemma~ef{lemma:unshielded-analog}). Then $q'$ must start with a directed edge, otherwise $q' \oplus r'$ would violate the b-amenability condition{}. Hence, $q'$ must be causal in~$\g$ (Lemma~ef{lemma:unshielded-edgeanalog}). Let $\g[D]$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$ that has no additional edges into $W$ as compared to $\g$ (Lemma~ef{lemma:no-new-into}). Then since $r'$ and $s'$ are unshielded and b-possibly causal, the paths corresponding to $r'$ and $s'$ in $\g[D]$ are causal (or of zero length). Hence, $V \in  fb{\g[D]}$, so that $\mathbf{Z} \cap  fb{\g[D]} 
eq \emptyset$.

$\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-forbidden set condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in $\g$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.3
nodes.statement:
This lemma is related to Lemma~10 from \cite{perkovic16},but instead of using Lemma 52 from \cite{perkovic16}, we use Lemma~ef{lemma:2-pdag}. To prove $
eg$~ef{l:eqb1-pdag}$\Rightarrow
eg$~ef{l:eqb3-pdag} let $p$ be a proper b-non-causal definite status path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ that is d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$ in~$\g$. The path corresponding to $p$ in any $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$ is proper, non-causal (Lemma~ef{lemma:posdir-path}) and d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$. The implication $
eg$~ef{l:eqb3-pdag}$\Rightarrow
eg$~ef{l:eqb2-pdag} trivially holds, so it is only left to prove that $
eg$~ef{l:eqb2-pdag}$\Rightarrow
eg$~ef{l:eqb1-pdag}. Thus, assume there is a $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$ such that a proper b-non-causal path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ in~$\g[D]$ is d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$. Among the shortest proper non-causal paths from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ that are d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$ in~$\g[D]$, choose a path $p$ with a minimal $distance-from-\!{\mathbf{Z}}$ (Definition~ef{def:distance from Z}). Let $\pstar$ in $\g$ be the path corresponding to $p$ in $\g[D]$. By Lemma~ef{lemma:2-pdag}, $\pstar$ is a proper b-non-causal definite status path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ that is d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Cycle of contrapositives; the hard step picks a shortest d-connecting non-causal path of minimal distance-from-$\mathbf{Z}$ in a DAG and applies Lemma C.6.

nodes.name: Shortcuts of d-connecting non-causal paths stay b-non-causal
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. Let $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfy the b-amenability condition{} and the b-forbidden set condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\g$. Let $\g[D]$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$ and let $p = \langle X = V_{0}, V_{1},\dots ,V_{k} = Y \rangle, k \ge 1,$ be a proper non-causal path from $X \in \mathbf{X}$ to $Y \in \mathbf{Y}$ that is d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$ in~$\g[D]$. Let $\pstar$ in~$\g$ denote the path corresponding to $p$. Then: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item Let $i,j \in \mathbb{N}, 0 < i < j \leq k,$ such that there is an edge $\langle V_i, V_j \rangle$ in~$\g$. The path $ \pstar(X,V_i) \oplus \langle V_i, V_j \rangle \oplus \pstar(V_j,Y)$ ($\pstar(V_j, Y)$ is possibly of zero length) is a proper b-non-causal path in~$\g$. For $j=i+1$, this implies that $\pstar$ is a proper b-non-causal path. \item If $X \leftarrow V_1$ and $V_1 \rightarrow V_2$ are not in $\g$ and there is an edge $\langle X,V_2 \rangle$ in $\g$, then $\pstar[q]=\langle X,V_2 \rangle \oplus \pstar(V_2,Y)$, ($\pstar(V_2, Y)$ is possibly of zero length) is a proper b-non-causal path in~$\g$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Chord-shortcuts of a d-connecting proper non-causal path remain proper b-non-causal in $\g$, under b-amenability and the forbidden-set condition.

Let $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfy the b-amenability condition{} and the b-forbidden set condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\g$.
Let $i,j \in \mathbb{N}, 0 < i < j \leq k,$ such that there is an edge $\langle V_i, V_j \rangle$ in~$\g$.

Let $i,j \in \mathbb{N}, 0 < i < j \leq k,$ such that there is an edge $\langle V_i, V_j \rangle$ in~$\g$.

nodes.label: lemma:non-causal-path-pdag

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.4
nodes.statement: This lemma is related to Lemma 50 from \cite{perkovic16}. In particular, \ref{l:ncp:pdag} in Lemma~\ref{lemma:non-causal-path-pdag} and (i) in Lemma 50 from \cite{perkovic16} and their proofs match. The result in \ref{l:ncp:b-pdag-new} differs in both statement and proof from (ii)-(iii) in Lemma 50 from \cite{perkovic16}. All paths considered are proper as they are subsequences of $\pstar$, which corresponds to $p$. \ref{l:ncp:pdag} We use proof by contradiction. Thus, suppose that $\pstar[q] = \pstar(X,V_i) \oplus \langle V_i, V_j \rangle \oplus \pstar(V_j,Y) $ is b-possibly causal in~$\g$. Then $\{V_1,\dots,V_i,V_j,\dots,V_k\} \subseteq \bfb{\g}$. Since $\g$ is b-amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$, $\pstar[q]$ and $\pstar(X,V_i)$ as well must start with $X \rightarrow V_1$. Then $p$ also starts with $X \rightarrow V_1$ and since $p$ is non-causal, there is at least one collider on $p$. Let $V_r, r \ge 1,$ be the collider closest to $X$ on $p$, then $V_r \in \bfb{\g[D]}$. Since $p$ is d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$, $\mathbf{Z} \cap \mathrm{De}(V_r,\g[D]) \neq \emptyset$. Since $\mathrm{De}(V_r,\g[D]) \subseteq \bfb{\g[D]}$ and since $\bfb{\g[D]} \subseteq \bfb{\g}$, this contradicts $\mathbf{Z} \cap \bfb{\g} = \emptyset$. \ref{l:ncp:b-pdag-new} We again use proof by contradiction. Suppose neither $X \leftarrow V_1$ nor $V_1 \rightarrow V_2$ are in $\g$ and $\pstar[q]$ is a b-possibly causal path. Since $\g$ is b-amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$, $X \to V_2$ is in~$\g$ and $\{V_2,\dots,V_k\} \subseteq \bfb{\g}$. Since $V_1 \rightarrow V_2$ is not in $\g$, either $V_1 - V_2$ or $V_1\leftarrow V_2$ is in $\g$. Hence, $V_1 \in b-PossDe(V_2,\g)$. Since $b-PossDe(V_2,\g) \subseteq \bfb{\g}$, it follows that $V_1 \in \bfb{\g}$. Suppose that $V_1 \leftarrow V_2$ is in $\g$. Then $X \rightarrow V_2 \rightarrow V_1$ and rule $R2$ implies that $X \rightarrow V_1$ is in $\g$. Then $X \rightarrow V_1 \leftarrow V_2$, so since $p$ is d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$, $\mathbf{Z} \cap \mathrm{De}(V_1,\g[D]) \neq \emptyset$. But $\mathrm{De}(V_1,\g[D]) \subseteq b-PossDe(V_1,\g) \subseteq \bfb{\g}$, which contradicts that $\mathbf{Z} \cap \bfb{\g} = \emptyset$. Otherwise, $V_1 -V_2$ is in $\g$. Additionally, $X \rightarrow V_2$ is in $\g$ and $\pstar(V_2,Y)$ is b-possibly causal. So since $\pstar$ is b-non-causal (from \ref{l:ncp:pdag}), $X \leftarrow V_1$ must be in $\g$. This contradicts our assumption in \ref{l:ncp:b-pdag-new}.
nodes.statement_short: Both parts by contradiction: a b-possibly causal shortcut would put a d-connecting collider's descendants in the forbidden set.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.6
nodes.statement:
This lemma is related to Lemma~52 from \cite{perkovic16}. The line of reasoning used in this first part of this proof overlaps with the proof of Lemma~52. We will point out where the two proofs diverge. From Lemma~ef{lemma:1-pdag} we know that $\pstar$ is a proper b-non-causal definite status path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ in $\g$. We only need to prove that it is also d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$ in $\g$. Since $p$ is d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$ in $\g[D]$ and $\pstar$ is of definite status, it follows that no definite non-collider on $\pstar$ is in $\mathbf{Z}$ and that every collider on $\pstar$ has a possible descendant in $\mathbf{Z}$ (Lemma~ef{lemma:non-causal-path-pdag}). Since every collider on $\pstar$ has a b-possibly causal path to $\mathbf{Z}$, by Lemma~ef{lemma:unshielded-analog} there is b-possibly causal definite status path from every collider on $\pstar$ to a node in $\mathbf{Z}$. Let $C$ be an arbitrary collider on $\pstar$ and let $\pstar[d]$ be a shortest b-possibly causal definite status path from $C$ to a node in $\mathbf{Z}$. It is only left to show that $\pstar[d]$ is causal in $\g$, since then $C \in \mathrm{An}(\mathbf{Z},\g)$. If $\pstar[d]$ starts with a directed edge out of $C$, then $\pstar[d]$ is causal in $\g$ (Lemma~ef{lemma:unshielded-edgeanalog}). nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.6
nodes.statement: This theorem is related to Theorem~14 from \cite{perkovic16}. This proof relies on similar line of reasoning however since Theorem~14 from \cite{perkovic16} states a somewhat different result and relies on a few lemmas for the proof, we do not make a direct comparison between the two as we did with the result presented in Section~\ref{sec:proofadjust-mpdag}. We only need to prove that if there is a set that satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$, then $\badjustb{\g}$ also satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$. Hence, assume that $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$ and that $\badjustb{\g}$ does not satisfy the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$. We will show that this leads to a contradiction. Since $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g$ (Theorem~\ref{theorem:gac-pdag}), $\g$ is b-amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$. By construction $\badjustb{\g}$ satisfies the b-forbidden set condition{}, so it must violate the b-blocking condition{}. Let $p =\langle X = V_{0}, V_{1},\dots ,V_{k} = Y \rangle, k \ge 1, X \in \mathbf{X}, Y \in \mathbf{Y}$ be a shortest proper b-non-causal definite status paths from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ in $\g$ that is d-connecting given $\badjustb{\g}$. Since $\mathbf{Z}$ blocks $p$, $k >1$. So there is at least one non-endpoint node on $p$. Since $p$ is d-connecting given $\badjustb{\g}$ and $\badjustb{\g} = b-PossAn(\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y}, \g)\setminus(\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y} \cup \bfb{\g})$ any collider on $p$ is in $b-PossAn(\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y}, \g)$. Additionally, no collider $C$ on $p$ is in $\bfb{\g}$ otherwise, $\mathrm{De}(C,\g) \subseteq \bfb{\g}$ and $\bfb{\g} \cap \badjustb{\g} = \emptyset$ contradicts that $p$ is d-connecting given $\badjustb{\g}$. Thus, every collider on $p$ is in $b-PossAn(\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y}, \g) \setminus \bfb{\g}$. Any definite non-collider on $p$ is a b-possible ancestor of $X$, $Y$ or a collider on $p$. Hence, any definite non-collider on $p$ is in $b-PossAn(\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y},\g)$. Since $p$ is d-connecting given $\badjustb{\g}$, no definite non-collider on $p$ is in $\badjustb{\g}$. Then since $\badjustb{\g} = b-PossAn(\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y}, \g)\setminus(\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y} \cup \bfb{\g})$, every definite non-collider on $p$ is in $\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y} \cup \bfb{\g}$. Since $p$ is proper, no definite non-collider on $p$ is in $\mathbf{X}$. Additionally, if there was a definite non-collider $V$ on $p$ such that $V \in \mathbf{Y} \setminus \bfb{\g}$, then $p(X,V)$ would be a shorter proper b-non-causal definite status path in $\g$ that is d-connecting given $\badjustb{\g}$. Hence, any definite non-collider on $p$ must be in $\bfb{\g}$. Suppose that there is no collider on $p$. Then since $\mathbf{Z}$ blocks $p$, a non-collider on $p$ must be in $\mathbf{Z}$. This contradicts that $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-forbidden set condition{}. Thus, there is a collider on $p$ so let $V_{i-1} \rightarrow V_{i} \leftarrow V_{i+1}$ be a subpath of $p$. If there is a definite non-collider on $p$, then $V_{i-1}$ or $V_{i+1}$ is a non-collider on $p$. Suppose without loss of generality that $V_{i-1}$ is a definite non-collider on $p$. Then $V_{i-1} \in \bfb{\g}$. Since $V_{i-1} \rightarrow V_i$ is in $\g$, $V_i \in \bfb{\g}$, which contradicts that $V_i$ is a collider on $p$. Thus, there is no definite non-collider on $p$. Since there is at least one collider on $p$ and no definite non-collider is on $p$, it follows that $p$ is of the form $ X \rightarrow V_1 \leftarrow Y$ in $\g$. Since $V_1 \in b-PossAn(\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y},\g) \setminus \bfb{\g}$, let $q$ be a shortest b-possibly causal definite status path from $V_1$ to a node in $\mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y}$. Then $q = \langle V_1, \dots , V\rangle$, for some $V \in \mathbf{X} \cup \mathbf{Y}$. Then $V \in \mathbf{X}$ otherwise, $V_1 \in \bfb{\g} $. Thus, $r = (-p)(Y,V_1) \oplus q$ is a b-possibly causal path, so let $r'$ be an unshielded subsequence of $r$ that forms a b-possibly causal path from $Y$ to $\mathbf{X}$ in $\g$. Since $(-r)$ is a proper path with respect to $\mathbf{X}$, $(-r')$ is also a proper path with respect to $\mathbf{X}$. Then $(-r')$ must be a b-non-causal path otherwise, $Y \in \bfb{\g}$ which also implies $V_1 \in \bfb{\g}$. Since $r'$ is also unshielded, $(-r')$ is a proper b-non-causal definite status path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ in $\g$. Thus, $\mathbf{Z}$ must block $(-r')$. Since $r'$ is b-possibly causal, $(-r')$ does not contain a collider, so a definite non-collider on $(-r')$ must be in $\mathbf{Z}$. However, all definite non-colliders on $(-r')$ are also on $q$, so $\mathbf{Z}$ cannot block both $(-r')$ and $p$ in $\g$.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a shortest path d-connecting given $b$-Adjust is forced to the form $X\to V_1\leftarrow Y$, which then yields a path $\mathbf{Z}$ cannot block together with $p$.

nodes.name: Soundness direction
nodes.statement: Suppose first that $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in the maximal $\mathrm{PDAG}${} $\g$. We need to show that $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set (Definition~\ref{defadjustmentmpdag}) relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in every $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$. By applying Lemmas~\ref{lemma:amen-pdag},~\ref{lemma:eqpdag} and~\ref{lemma:eqb-pdag} in turn, it directly follows that $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in any $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$. Since the b-adjustment criterion reduces to the adjustment criterion \citep{shpitser2012validity,shpitser2012avalidity} in $\mathrm{DAG}$s and the adjustment criterion is sound for $\mathrm{DAG}$s, $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g[D]$.

Then by Lemma~\ref{lemma:amen-pdag}, there is no adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\g$. Otherwise, suppose $\g$ is b-amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$. Then $\mathbf{Z}$ violates the b-forbidden set condition{} or \expandafter\ignorespaces the b-blocking condition{}. We need to show $\mathbf{Z}$ is not an adjustment set in at least one $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$. Suppose $\mathbf{Z}$ violates \expandafter\ignorespaces the forbidden set condition. Then by Lemma~\ref{lemma:eqpdag}, it follows that there exists a $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$ such that $\mathbf{Z}$ does not satisfy the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g[D]$. Since the b-adjustment criterion reduces to the adjustment criterion \citep{shpitser2012validity,shpitser2012avalidity} in $\mathrm{DAG}$s and the adjustment criterion is complete for $\mathrm{DAG}$s, it follows that $\mathbf{Z}$ is not an adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g[D]$. Otherwise, suppose $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies \expandafter\ignorespaces the forbidden set condition, but violates \expandafter\ignorespaces the b-blocking condition{}. Then by Lemma~\ref{lemma:eqb-pdag}, it follows that there is a $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\g[D]$ in $[\g]$ such that $\mathbf{Z}$ does not satisfy the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in~$\g[D]$. nodes.name: Plan: two DAGs with incompatible adjustment sets
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\g$ violates the b-amenability condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$. We will show that in this case one can find $\mathrm{DAG}$s $\g[D]_1$ and $\g[D]_2$ in $[\g]$, such that there is no set that satisfies the b-adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in both $\g[D]_1$ and $\g[D]_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Plan: two DAGs with incompatible adjustment sets

nodes.name: Pick a shortest offending path $q'$
nodes.statement: Since $\g$ is not b-amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$, there is a proper b-possibly causal path $\pstar[q]$ from a node $X \in \mathbf{X}$ to a node $Y \in \mathbf{Y}$ that starts with a undirected edge. Let $\pstar[q'] = \langle X= V_0,V_1,\dots,V_k=Y\rangle, k \ge 1$ (where $V_1 = Y$ is allowed) be a shortest subsequence of $\pstar[q]$ such that $\pstar[q']$ is also a proper b-possibly causal path that starts with a undirected edge in~$\g$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick a shortest offending path $q'$

nodes.name: Definite status case: causal in one DAG, collider-free non-causal in another
nodes.statement: Suppose first that $\pstar[q']$ is of definite status in $\g$. Let $\g[D]_1$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$ that contains $X \rightarrow V_1$ and let $\g[D]_2$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $[\g]$ that has no additional edges into $V_1$ as compared to $\g$ (Lemma~\ref{lemma:no-new-into}). Then the path corresponding to $\pstar[q']$ in $\g[D]_1$ is causal, whereas the path corresponding to $\pstar[q']$ in $\g[D]_2$ is b-non-causal and contains no colliders. Hence, no set can satisfy both the b-forbidden set condition{} in $\g[D]_1$ and the b-blocking condition{} in $\g[D]_2$ relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$.
nodes.statement_short: Definite status case: causal in one DAG, collider-free non-causal in another

nodes.name: Non-definite status case (new for maximal PDAGs)
nodes.statement: Otherwise, $\pstar[q']$ is not of definite status in $\g$. In the proof of Lemma 8 from \cite{perkovic16}, the authors show that if $\pstar[q']$ is not of definite status, this leads to a contradiction. However, $\pstar[q']$ can be of non-definite status in $\g$ and this is where the proofs diverge. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:unshielded-analog}, $\pstar[q'](V_1,Y)$ must be unshielded and hence, of definite status in $\g$, since otherwise we can choose a shorter b-possibly causal path. Since $\pstar[q']$ is not of definite status and $\pstar[q'](V_1,Y)$ is of definite status, it follows that $V_1$ is not of definite status on $\pstar[q']$. Then $\langle X, V_1, V_2 \rangle$ is a shielded triple. By choice of $\pstar[q']$, $X - V_1$ is in $\g$. Additionally, since $V_1$ is not of definite status on $\pstar[q']$, $V_1 - V_2$ must be in $\g$. This implies that $X - V_1 -V_2$ is in $\g$ and $X \in \mathrm{Adj}(V_2,\g)$. Moreover, we must have $X \to V_2$, since $X - V_2$ contradicts the choice of $\pstar[q']$, and $X \leftarrow V_2$ contradicts that $\pstar[q']$ is b-possibly causal in $\g$. Let $\g[D]_1$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $\g$ that has no additional edges into $V_1$ as compared to $\g$ (Lemma~\ref{lemma:no-new-into}). Let $q_1$ be the path corresponding to $\pstar[q']$ in $\g[D]_1$. Then $q_1$ is of the form $X \leftarrow V_1 \rightarrow V_2 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow Y$ in $\g[D]_1$. Since $X \rightarrow V_2 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow Y$ is a proper causal path in $\g[D]_1$, $\{V_2, \dots, V_{k-1}\} \subseteq \bfb{\g[D]_{1}}$. Hence, any set that satisfies the b-blocking condition{} and the b-forbidden set condition{} relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g[D]_{1}$ must contain $V_1$ and not $\{V_2,\dots,V_{k-1}$. Let $\g[D]_2$ be a $\mathrm{DAG}$ in $\g$ that has no additional edges into $V_2$ as compared to $\g$ (Lemma~\ref{lemma:no-new-into}). Let $q_2$ be the path corresponding to $\pstar[q']$ in $\g[D]_2$. Since $X \rightarrow V_2 \rightarrow V_1$ is in $\g[D]_2$, $X \rightarrow V_1$ is in $\g[D]_2$ (Rule $R2$). Then $q_2$ is of the form $ X \rightarrow V_1 \leftarrow V_2 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow Y$ in $\g[D]_2$. Hence, any set that satisfies the b-forbidden set condition{} and the b-blocking condition{} {} relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g[D]_{1}$, violates the b-blocking condition{} {} relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ in $\g[D]_{2}$.

Then $V \in b-PossDe(W,\g)$ for some $W= V_i$ on a proper b-possibly causal path $p = \langle X=V_0, V_1,\dots, V_k=Y \rangle, 1 \le i \le k$ from $X \in \mathbf{X}$ to $Y \in \mathbf{Y}$. Hence, $V \in \bfb{\g[D]}$, so that $\mathbf{Z} \cap \bfb{\g[D]} \neq \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Choose a minimal one and apply Lemma C.6
nodes.statement: Among the shortest proper non-causal paths from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ that are d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$ in~$\g[D]$, choose a path $p$ with a minimal $distance-from-\!{\mathbf{Z}}$ (Definition~\ref{def:distance from Z}). Let $\pstar$ in $\g$ be the path corresponding to $p$ in $\g[D]$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:2-pdag}, $\pstar$ is a proper b-non-causal definite status path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ that is d-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$.

nodes.name: Relation to Lemma 50 of Perkovic et al.
nodes.statement: This lemma is related to Lemma 50 from \cite{perkovic16}. In particular, \ref{l:ncp:pdag} in Lemma~\ref{lemma:non-causal-path-pdag} and (i) in Lemma 50 from \cite{perkovic16} and their proofs match. The result in \ref{l:ncp:b-pdag-new} differs in both statement and proof from (ii)-(iii) in Lemma 50 from \cite{perkovic16}.
